findings.where: 'Where we're starting' section: the Canggu, Uluwatu and Kuta Lombok destination cards, and the 'Best hostels ›' line in each
findings.fault: The cards look clickable, but nothing happens when you click them. Each one is a white card with a chevron 'Best hostels' line in link colour and a hover effect. The parts map lists all three as static, so there is no link to any destination guide anywhere on the page. Sending visitors to the guides is one of the page's three jobs, and both 'Explore destinations' and the nav's 'Destinations' lead only to these dead cards.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who taps 'Explore destinations' and then 'Canggu' expecting the hostel guide. Nothing happens, so the page looks broken, and the visitor can't reach the one piece of real content the site has before launch.

findings.where: Nav 'How we rank'; footer 'Privacy', 'Terms', 'How we rank' and 'Report content'
findings.fault: Each of these links points back to this same page. 'How we rank' promises an explanation of the merit ranking, which is the product's main claim. Privacy and Terms promise legal pages. None of them exist, and clicking just reloads the homepage.
findings.who_objects: A visitor deciding whether to trust a new 'ranked on merit alone' site who clicks 'How we rank' to check the claim, and anyone looking for the privacy terms before sending their email address. Both land back where they started and may conclude the site is a shell.

findings.where: Hero: the eyebrow 'The better way to find hostels in Indonesia.', the wordmark-as-headline and the body paragraph
findings.fault: The biggest type in the hero is just the brand name, which the nav bar already shows. What the site actually does is in a small eyebrow and a paragraph of small body text: ranking hostels on merit alone, then sending you to book with the hostel. 'The better way' is a vague claim, and the specific reason to care is the thing set smallest.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor on a phone giving the page five seconds. They see a logo twice and have to read the fine print to learn why this differs from the booking site they already use.

findings.fault: This section heading is set much larger than the hero headline. At about 120 px on desktop it fills the screen and becomes the loudest thing on the page, louder than the brand line and the primary action.
findings.who_objects: A visitor scrolling past the hero, who reads a giant label for three small cards as the page's main point. The size hierarchy says 'where we're starting' matters more than what MantaHostels is.

findings.fault: The cards have a thick purple border and a large soft drop shadow at rest. Purple is not in the palette. The rules file sets cards in sand-border at 1 to 1.5 px and says nothing sits at rest under a heavy shadow. The cards look as if they belong to another site.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose brand sheet assigns every colour one job and has no purple. Visitors also see a section styled unlike everything else on the page.

findings.where: Destination cards: the region eyebrow (BALI, LOMBOK) and the place names
findings.fault: The eyebrows and place names are set in a monospace typewriter face. The brand uses Quicksand for headings and Nunito Sans for labels. The mono face reads like code and drops the beachy brand voice exactly where the destinations are named.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose type system is binding. To a backpacker, the place names look like placeholder or developer text rather than a travel guide.

findings.where: Hero: the coral 'Email luc@mantahostels.com for launch news' button and the 'Explore destinations' button below it
findings.fault: The two buttons have unrelated shapes. The coral one is a full pill and the outline one has square corners. The rules file sets both buttons to the 8 px control radius, and the house reserves pill shapes for badges and chips. Side by side, the pair looks like it came from two different kits.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose button components fix one control radius. Visitors also see two buttons that don't look like they belong to one set.

findings.where: Hero primary action 'Email luc@mantahostels.com for launch news' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The launch-news sign-up is a mailto link with a whole sentence, including the full address, as its label. On a phone the label wraps onto two lines inside the pill. The visitor has to open a mail app and write an email themselves to sign up, and nothing tells them what to write.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker mid-trip on a phone with webmail only or no mail app set up. The tap opens nothing useful or an empty message, so many give up instead of signing up for launch news.

findings.where: Nav bar: 'Destinations' next to 'How we rank'
findings.fault: The two nav links are treated differently. 'How we rank' is underlined and 'Destinations' is not, with no reason a visitor can see. It reads as if one is the current page or a different kind of link.
findings.who_objects: A visitor scanning the nav, who can't tell why one item is marked out. The rules file reserves a changed treatment in the nav for the current page.

findings.where: Desktop layout: the hero text column against the 'Where we're starting' heading and the cards
findings.fault: The hero content starts at one left edge, about 424 px in. The next section's heading and cards start at a different edge, about 195 px, matching the nav wordmark. The page has two left edges with no visible reason, which breaks the continuity from the hero into the content.
findings.who_objects: A visitor reading top to bottom, whose eye has to jump sideways between sections. The page looks unfinished.

findings.where: Footer line 'Launching across Indonesia · piloting now in Bali' against the Lombok card in 'Where we're starting'
findings.fault: The footer says the pilot is in Bali, but the section above lists Kuta Lombok as a starting place. The page contradicts itself about where the service covers.
findings.who_objects: A traveller heading to Lombok, who can't tell whether Lombok is covered. On a site whose pitch is honesty, a self-contradiction weakens trust.
